raw_response:
Looking at my 225 mu, I need to manage four crops this year. My main system is wheat-maize rotation — that's the backbone, what I've been doing for 15 years and what my neighbors do. I'll put 140 mu into that rotation. The remaining 85 mu splits between chili and stevia, both cash crops I rely on for household income.

For wheat this winter, I'll plough deep before planting — I always do this on wheat fields, it breaks up the hardpan and helps with roots. I'll use an improved local variety, probably Jimai series, which performs well here in Quzhou. Three irrigations: winter watering in December to protect roots from frost, jointing in April, and grain fill in May. Fertilizer I'll apply as a split — base dressing before planting, then topdress at jointing.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll turn those same 140 mu over to summer maize right away. No time for deep tillage — I'll use rotary and plant within a week.郑单958 hybrid or similar, because it's reliable and my input dealer always has it. Maize needs a good tasseling irrigation or yield drops badly.

For chili, 50 mu on a separate block. Chili is labor-intensive and needs more water and pesticide attention than grain crops. I'll irrigate 6 times through the season — this crop cannot dry out. My family handles most of the labor but we'll hire help at harvest.

Stevia takes 35 mu. It's become worth growing in this area and the buyers come to us. I'll use transplants from the nursery, rotary tillage before transplanting, moderate fertilizer.
